<reason>Both sides argued with discipline and answered pressure questions cleanly in the required A1/A2 format, but B built the more cohesive and resilient case. B's reframing of the "price control fails" analogy (fixed stadium supply vs. bakeable bread) directly defused A's opening mechanism, and B's "feasibility, not redundancy" answer to A's app-lock dilemma held up better than A's rejoinder that resale fees uniquely "fund" the lock's infrastructure — a claim A never grounded concretely. Crucially, A's fallback solution (verified-fan presales plus dynamic pricing) was never fully insulated from B's recurring charge that this just lets "the platform scalp first," and A's closing dilemma ("pick one") never squarely engaged B's underlying market-power explanation for why platforms wouldn't voluntarily build a fair lane. B's nurse-vs-bot framing gave the debate a clearer, more memorable throughline that survived the exchange better than A's enforcement-migration story, which B directly answered by noting the black market A warns about already exists and is worse.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's answer to A's Pressure Q1 ("the tech is a switch platforms already own... it proves feasibility, not redundancy") most cleanly resolved the central app-lock dilemma A had built its case around, and A's follow-up (fees fund the lock) never fully recovered the point.</best_rebuttal>
